subject: SIG questionnaire — deployment responsibilities & dataflow summary
messages:
From: Elena Torres <security@acme-corp.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@acme-corp.com
Date: Tue, 04 May 2027 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: SIG: questions on Hosted/Dedicated/Private deployment responsibilities

Hi Rafael / Lauren,

Thanks for taking our SIG request. We've started mapping the controls and have a few open items specifically around "deployment ownership" (who holds keys, where model weights live, what access Redwood retains) and evidence artifacts we can rely on for the questionnaire. I've attached our spreadsheet with line items I'm asking about (see tab "DeploymentModes").

Top questions:
- For Hosted: who is the custodian of encryption keys for customer data and model cache?
- For Dedicated: are model weights or inference checkpoints ever copied to an S3 or storage controlled by Redwood?
- For Private/VPC/on-prem: do you provide any remote access for upgrades or is everything customer-managed?

We need clear, short answers we can paste into the SIG (control-level statements) and one diagram that shows data-in-motion and data-at-rest boundaries per deployment mode.

Can you also point us to evidence artifacts (audit log excerpts, diagram, KMS integration note) we can upload? Our deadline for the next procurement milestone is Friday.

Thanks — Elena
Elena Torres
Senior Security Analyst, Acme Corp

Subject: Re: SIG: questions on Hosted/Dedicated/Private deployment responsibilities

Elena —

Appreciate the clear spreadsheet. Below are concise, SIG-ready statements per deployment mode plus the artifacts we're attaching. I tried to keep the language short so you can paste into the questionnaire cells; let me know if you prefer slightly longer control-context text.

1) Hosted (Redwood-managed runtime)
- Statement: "Redwood operates a multi-tenant hosted inference service. Customer data in transit and at rest is encrypted; Redwood holds and rotates the runtime encryption keys by default. Customers may request BYOK (bring-your-own-key) options for select enterprise tiers."
- Data custody & keys: Runtime/KV cache keys are managed by Redwood for standard hosted customers; enterprise hosted customers can enable KMS integration (Redwood-managed policy with customer-provided keys in supported clouds).
- Model weights: Canonical model artifacts are hosted in Redwood storage; ephemeral caches of model segments used for serving are transient and deleted per retention policy. Model training artifacts are not retained by Redwood unless explicitly agreed.
- Evidence: redwood-sig-evidence-20270504.pdf (section A.1), audit-log-sample (available on request), kms-integration-note.txt

2) Dedicated (customer-dedicated GPU pools)
- Statement: "Dedicated provides isolated GPU capacity for a single customer; storage volumes for inference artifacts and tenant data are isolated and mounted per-customer. Key control integrates with customer KMS; Redwood does not access customer-managed keys."
- Data custody & keys: Customers can choose customer-managed KMS keys for encryption-at-rest on attached volumes and object storage. By default, Redwood offers managed keys but will enable BYOK on contract.
- Model weights: We can deploy customer-provided model weights to a customer-dedicated storage endpoint. Copies are limited to the dedicated environment and not mixed with other tenants.
- Evidence: redwood-sig-evidence-20270504.pdf (section B.2), deployment-diagram.png (dedicated flow)

3) Private (VPC / on-prem package)
- Statement: "Private deployments (VPC or on-prem) run under customer control: network, storage, and key management are managed by the customer. Redwood's control plane can be configured to have zero access; software upgrades and support access are performed under customer-approved access policies."
- Data custody & keys: Customer retains all keys in their KMS/HSM. No customer data or model weights leave the customer's environment unless explicitly exported by the customer.
- Model weights: Stored only in customer-controlled storage; Redwood does not persist weights in any Redwood-managed infrastructure in normal operation.
- Evidence: redwood-sig-evidence-20270504.pdf (section C.1), kms-integration-note.txt

Additional notes
- Auditing: All modes produce request/response logs and platform-level audit logs. For Hosted/Dedicated, tenant-level access logs can be provided as redacted extracts. For Private, audit logging is under customer control.
- Access & support: For Dedicated we maintain a support channel and can enable just-in-time (JIT) support tunnels with customer approval; for Private deployments remote access is only via customer-configured channels and requires explicit authorization.

Attachments included for the SIG response: redwood-sig-evidence-20270504.pdf (controls mapping), deployment-diagram.png (per-mode dataflow), kms-integration-note.txt (how BYOK works). I'll also place a short control-to-evidence mapping in the Drive link and paste snippets you can use.

Next steps: I can prepare two short paste-ready control-statements per SIG question and upload to your spreadsheet if you'd like. If you can flag the rows in tab "DeploymentModes" that need the exact text, we'll populate them.

-Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: SIG: questions on Hosted/Dedicated/Private deployment responsibilities

Thanks Rafael — that's very helpful. A couple quick clarifications before we paste into the SIG:

- For Dedicated: can you confirm whether any automated backups of model weights are stored in a central Redwood S3 bucket (i.e., outside the dedicated tenant's storage)? If backups exist, are they encrypted with customer-managed keys?
- For Hosted: the statement about BYOK is useful — can you confirm which enterprise tiers support BYOK and whether there is any functional difference in runtime performance with BYOK enabled?

Also, procurement is asking for a single-page diagram that labels where customer secrets live and where Redwood staff could theoretically access logs or run-time metrics. The deployment-diagram.png looks good from the filename; can you confirm it will include those labels?

If you can drop a short one-line confirmation for the two bullets above we'll move forward.

—Elena
